title: Imaging Procedures for Small Animals at UC Davis
author: Douglas J. Rowland
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.678hhrw

steps.title: Prepare animals for PET, CT, or SPECT
steps.instruction: Prepare the animals based on the specific radiotracer and imaging requirements.

substeps.instruction: Fast mice or rats (water unrestricted) for up to 20 hours if required to improve radiotracer uptake.
If fiducial markers are required, shave the attachment regions and apply commercial hair removal cream briefly to remove stubble.

steps.title: Administer radiotracer
steps.instruction: Inject the selected radiotracer (see Radiotracer list) via iv, ip, or sc injection.

substeps.instruction: Ensure dose is <1 mCi for mice and <4 mCi for rats.
For conscious animals: briefly restrain in a commercial restrainer; optionally immerse tail in warm water for 30-60 seconds to increase vasodilation.

For catheter placement: clean tail with alcohol wipe and insert a catheter (mouse/rat: 28 ga or 30 ga needle on PE10 or MicroRenathane tubing; rat: 22 or 24 ga iv catheter) filled with heparinized saline into the tail vein.
Insert a needle/syringe or catheter plug into the catheter end until injection. Use a syringe shield to minimize radiation dose to personnel.

steps.title: Allow radiotracer uptake
steps.instruction: Wait for the radiotracer uptake period, typically 0.5 hr (range 0-2 hr), depending on the protocol.

substeps.instruction: Maintain the animal as conscious or continuously anesthetized.
If anesthetized, keep the animal warm using a heat lamp or heating device (e.g., Deltaphase pads).

steps.title: Perform PET, CT, or SPECT imaging
steps.instruction: Acquire images using the appropriate scanner.

substeps.instruction: Place the animal on plastic-backed absorbent paper to contain excreted urine.
Image via microPET or microSPECT (typically 10 min to 2 hr) or microCT (typically 10-30 min).
For microCT contrast: dose Fenestra at 0.2 ml/20 g in mice or 5-10 ml/kg in rats, following manufacturer recommendations for allowable injection volume.
If using fiducial markers, affix 2-3 low-radioactivity markers to the fur or skin using tape or glue (glue only if animal is to be euthanized).

steps.title: Perform MRI imaging
steps.instruction: Image the animal using the MRI scanner.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize the animal and place it inside the scanner.
Maintain body temperature using the imaging bed.
Image typically for up to 1 hour.

If contrast agents (e.g., gadolinium, paramagnetic gadolinium-containing liposomes, superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles) are used, inject iv (or ip if iv is difficult and ip absorption is known).

steps.title: Perform Optical imaging
steps.instruction: Image the animal using the Xenogen IVIS (bioluminescence) or Maestro 2 (fluorescence) system.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize the animal.
Shave anticipated signal regions and apply commercial hair removal cream briefly to remove stubble.

For bioluminescence: inject substrate for luciferase (luciferin, 150 mg/kg iv/ip or coelenterazine, 3 mg/kg iv/ip) via ip or iv. Place animal on a warmed surface in a light-tight box (IVIS chamber) and image with a CCD camera for typically 20 min or less.

For fluorescence: inject fluorescently-labeled murine antibody, microspheres, or red/near-infrared emitting optical contrast agent (iv, ip, sc, or im), or use animals/cells transfected with fluorescent proteins. Place animal on a warmed surface in a light-tight box and image with a CCD camera for seconds up to 60 minutes.
